adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh call was changed to use `refreshOAuthTokens(...)`. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, `refreshOAuthTokens` POSTs to the external sync endpoint and returns that `Response` instead of Lark’s native refresh response. However the Lark code still immediately passes that `resp` into `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>(resp, ...)`, i.e., it still expects Lark’s `RefreshTokenResp` shape. Unlike other integrations updated in this diff (e.g., Google/O365/Zoom) which added `parseRefreshTokenResponse` to tolerate a reduced token payload, Lark did not add any such parsing/normalization. Therefore, under sync mode, Lark’s refresh flow is very likely to break or produce missing fields (e.g., refresh token/refresh expiry) because the sync endpoint is explicitly documented in-code as returning only access token + expiry. The finding’s specific downstream deletion behavior isn’t shown in the diff, but the diff does introduce the underlying mismatch that would plausibly lead to it.
